Workbench
A sturdy workbench, freshly raised. There is nothing to make here yet.
Nothing for now.
Mind how you go.
Aye. Watch the road out.
Right. I have things to be doing.
Good day to you, then.
Something else.
What is this place?
You are in {town}. I keep the {trade} here.
{town}. I keep the {trade}, and I have never been anywhere else.
This is {town}. You want the {trade}, you want me.
{town}, and glad of it most days. The {trade} is mine.
Heard anything lately?
Nothing worth repeating.
Not a thing. It has been that sort of month.
You would be the first to hear it if there were.
Nothing. Ask me again when somebody does something.
Show me your wares.
I have things to sell.
Not today. Come back another time.
Not yet. Ask me again when I have something to show you.
I have nothing ready. Another day.
Not just now. There will be more here before long.

{name} watches you come the whole way in.
{name} looks you over and does not move.
{name} shifts a hand off the spear, then puts it back.
{name} has been standing here long enough to have noticed you twice.
{name} lets you get close before saying anything at all.
{name} sets something down and turns to you.
{name} waits, as though there were all day.
{name} finishes what they were saying under their breath first.
{name} looks up from the step they were sweeping.
{name} greets you by no name at all, and means it kindly.
{name} wipes both hands and looks up. 'What will it be?'
{name} is already talking before you reach the counter.
{name} finds you a place at the end of the bench without being asked.
{name} counts something twice, loses it, and turns to you anyway.
{name} has a look at your boots before your face.
{name} straightens up slowly and squints at you.
{name} keeps one eye on the weather while you speak.
{name} finishes the row before coming over.
{name} leans on the gate as though it were the plan all along.
{name} wipes both hands on the same patch of trouser.
{name} puts the load down. It looks like a relief.
{name} nods at you without stopping work.
{name} straightens up, hears something click, and ignores it.
{name} looks glad of any reason to stop.
{name} shouts something to somebody else first, then turns round.
{name} looks up quickly, then looks less hopeful.
{name} has been watching you since the corner.
{name} makes room on the step without being asked.
{name} says nothing and waits to see what you are.
{name} has a greeting ready and has clearly used it all morning.
{name} stares at you without blinking.
{name} appears at your elbow from nowhere.
{name} runs up, stops short, and thinks better of it.
{name} asks you three things before you get one in.
{name} is walking backwards in front of you now.
{name} looks up from a ledger and leaves a finger on the line.
{name} sets down what they were counting and gives you the counter.
{name} moves a crate off the counter with their knee.
{name} has already decided you are buying something.
{name} greets you like somebody who greets everybody.
{name} wipes flour off both hands before anything else.
{name} pushes the shutter wider to see you properly.
{name} is already halfway through the day and shows it.
{name} turns from the oven with the door still open behind them.
{name} smells of the morning and has the arms for it.
{name} steps out of the noise to hear you.
{name} is grey to the elbow and does not seem to mind.
{name} waves you back from the running stone first.
{name} listens with their head tilted, out of habit.
{name} shouts a greeting, then remembers you are close enough.
What is it you do here?
The {trade}. Walk it, stand in it, walk it again.
I keep the {trade}. Most days that means being seen and nothing else.
The {trade}. It is standing still for money, and I am good at it.
I am on the {trade}. Nobody thanks you for the nights nothing happens.
The {trade}, since I was old enough to carry the spear.
The {trade} is mine to keep. People come when they need to.
I keep the {trade}. Somebody has to, and nobody else offered.
The {trade}, and everything that comes with it. Mostly it is listening.
I have the {trade}. It was here before me and it will outlast me.
The {trade}. People think that means quiet. It means sweeping.
The {trade}. Beds, beer, and listening to people who have had both.
I keep the {trade}. You hear everything twice and half of it is true.
The {trade}. I am up before the bakers and down after the drunks.
I have the {trade} off my mother. She had it off hers.
The {trade}. Everyone brings their business through it and none of it is mine.
The {trade}, same as my father. The work does not change much.
I work the {trade}. Ask me again after harvest and I may be happier.
The {trade}. It is the same year over and over and never the same twice.
I have the {trade} out past the wall. They are enough to keep me tired.
The {trade}. My grandfather cleared them and I have not improved on it.
The {trade}, mostly. Some weeks that is stone, some weeks it is sacks.
Whatever the {trade} wants doing. I am not fussy and it does not ask.
The {trade} pays me and I do not ask it many questions.
I am at the {trade}. It is not skilled and it is not light.
The {trade}, since I was fourteen. It is honest and it is heavy.
The {trade} is what I have. It is not much of a trade.
I sit. People walk past. That is the whole of it.
I keep the {trade} and the {trade} keeps me. Barely.
The {trade}. Nobody is queueing to take it off me.
This. What you are looking at. There is no second part to it.
{trade}. That is what they tell me when I ask, anyway.
Nothing yet. I am meant to be helping but I am not.
{trade}, yet. When I am bigger I am going to be the one with the horses.
I help. Sometimes. When somebody is watching.
{trade}. It is very important and I am very busy.
The {trade}. A bit of everything, and never enough of whatever you came for.
I keep the {trade}. What I have is what came up the road.
The {trade}. I make nothing, which is why I have some of all of it.
The {trade}, and the ledger that goes with it.
I run the {trade}. Ask, and if it is not on the shelf I will tell you plainly.
The {trade}. Up before the town, done before the afternoon.
I keep the {trade}. One day of bread a day, and no more than that.
The {trade}. It is hot work that nobody thinks about until it stops.
I am the {trade} here. The flour comes to me and the town comes after it.
The {trade}. Bread does not keep, so I am never ahead and never behind.
The {trade}. Grain in at one end, flour out at the other.
I keep the {trade}. Everything the town eats comes past this stone first.
The {trade}. Loud, dusty, and the only one of me for some way.
I work the {trade}. The wheel decides the hours, not I.
The {trade}. I take a share of what I grind, which is how a mill lives.

How old is {place}?
The {civ} laid the first stones of {place} {era}, around the year {year}. We have been here ever since.
{place} goes back {era} - {year} or near enough - when the {civ} came up the valley and stopped.
Somebody had to be first. The {civ}, {era}, and {place} has been here since.
Why the walls?
{place} put its walls up {era}. Around {year}, and nobody builds walls for the first fright.
Somebody frightened {place} badly enough to pay for stone. {era}, and they have never taken them down.
Has {place} ever been taken?
The {civ} came through {place} {era} and took what they liked. The {foe} could not hold it.
Around {year}. The {civ} in the streets of {place}, and whatever the {foe} promised, no help coming.
{place} has been taken once, {era}. People here have long memories about the {civ}.
What became of {place}?
They pulled {place} down {era}, somewhere around {year}. Nothing was rebuilt.
There is nothing at {place} now. {era} somebody made sure of it, and nobody argued afterwards.
Why did {place} empty out?
{place} emptied {era}. People left one household at a time, and then there was nobody.
Nobody drove them out of {place}. They just stopped seeing a reason to stay, {era}.
What happened at {place}?
The blight took the fields at {place}, and {era} - about {year} - there was no reason left to stay.
What happened to {place}?
The mountain took {place} {era}, around {year}. You can still walk into what is left of it.
Ash. All of it, in one night, {era}. {place} is under there somewhere.
{place} is down there. Everything above it is what the mountain put there {era}.
Who are the {civ}?
The {civ} count their beginning from about {year}, at {place}. {era}, if that means more to you.
Ask the {civ} and they will start at {place}, {era}. They will take a while about it.
Whatever happened to the {civ}?
The {civ} came apart {era}, around {year}. There is nobody left to answer for them.
You will not find the {civ} to ask. They were gone {era} and took their records with them.
Has there been war?
The {civ} declared on the {foe} {era}, near enough {year}. It went on longer than anyone promised.
The {civ} and the {foe} stopped pretending {era}. Everyone saw it coming and nobody stopped it.
Any fighting near here?
The {civ} and the {foe} fought here {era}. The ground still turns up iron if you dig.
Around {year}, {era}. A bad day for the {foe}, a good one for the {civ}, and a worse one for whoever was farming it.
Do not plough the far field. The {civ} and the {foe} left things in it {era}.
Was {place} ever besieged?
The {civ} sat outside {place} for the best part of a year, {era}, waiting for hunger to do the work.
{place} was shut up for the best part of a year, {era}. The {civ} only had to wait.
Who holds {place} now?
The {civ} took {place} {era} - about {year} - and kept it.
{place} belongs to the {civ} now. It has {era}, whatever the old people call it.
Is there peace?
The {civ} and the {foe} signed {era}, around {year}. It has held, more or less.
There has been no fighting since {era}. The {civ} and the {foe} both say they won.
Has sickness come through?
Plague in {place}, {era}. They burned the clothes and it went on spreading anyway.
Around {year} was the sickness. Ask anybody old enough and they will tell you who they lost.
Nobody can give you a clean year. Around {year}, and {place} lost a third of itself.
Have the harvests ever failed?
{place} went hungry {era}, about {year}. Two bad harvests together is all it takes.
{era} there was nothing in {place} to eat. People remember who shared and who did not.
Does the water ever come up?
The water came into {place} {era}, around {year}. It has come close since, but not like that.
The river had {place} {era}. You can still see the line on the walls if you know to look.
Is that mountain safe?
The mountain woke {era}, somewhere around {year}. Ash on everything for a season.
{era}. You could read by the light of it at midnight, and nobody slept.
The air was wrong for a whole season, {era}. Everything we grew that year tasted of it.
Who leads the {civ}?
{figure} came up among the {civ} {era}, around the year {year}.
Everything you hear about the {civ} {era} comes back to {figure} sooner or later.
What became of {figure}?
{figure} of the {civ} died {era}, in bed, which is more than most get.
How did {figure} die?
{figure} of the {civ} fell in battle {era}. About {year}, if you want it written down.
{figure} did not come home. The {civ} lost them {era} and have not stopped saying so.
Is the road safe?
{figure} of the {civ} went out into the waste {era} and never came back.
Around {year}. {figure} took the short way across and is buried wherever they fell.
{figure} of the {civ} is out there somewhere, {era}. People still say they saw a light.
Did anyone go and look?
{figure} walked out to the wound {era}. No grave, no word, nothing.
Is anything famous made near here?
{figure} made {artifact} {era}. Around {year}, they say, though they would.
Who carries {artifact}?
{artifact} passed to {figure} {era}. Not everyone thought it should have.
Was anything ever lost around here?
Something went missing {era} that people still come asking after. Nobody agrees where.
Where did {artifact} end up?
{artifact} went into the ground with {figure} {era}, around {year}.
Is there anything worth digging for?
The {civ} opened the workings above {place} {era}, around {year}. It changed what this country is for.
Is there a house of the faith nearby?
The {civ} founded the house out past {place} {era} - somewhere poor and hard to reach, as they do.
Who watches the frontier?
There is a fort on the high ground above {place}. The {civ} put it there {era}, around {year}.
What is the light on the headland?
The light stands off {place}. The {civ} first lit it {era} and it has not been dark since.
What is that stone for?
The {civ} raised it over {place} {era}, about {year}. Everybody argues about what it means.
Has anything changed in your lifetime?
The {civ} worked something new out {era}, around {year}, and the work has been easier since.
Work here is not what it was. Something the {civ} worked out {era}, and nobody went back.
Where did the mana come from?
Something came down {era} - {year}, they reckon. Everything strange in this world starts there.
What is wrong with the land?
The corruption reached the fields at {place} {era}, about {year}. It does not go back.
Why is {place} still standing?
The {civ} raised wards at {place} {era}. That is the only reason anybody is still there.
What do people here believe?
The {civ} swore themselves at {place} {era}, around {year}, and meant it.
Was there ever a falling out over it?
The {civ} broke with what they had sworn, at {place}, {era}. It is still not forgiven.
What is the stone circle?
The {civ} raised it above {place} {era}, around {year}, to work at.
Do they still hold the rites?
The {civ} kept the rite {era}, about {year}. They keep it still, when it matters.
Quiet shift?
Quiet is the whole job. A shift you remember is a shift that went wrong.
So far. I have learned not to say it out loud before sundown.
Quiet. Four hours of it, and four more after that.
Nothing yet. That is not luck, that is two of us standing here.
You look tired.
New boots. Everyone says they wear in. Nobody says how long that takes.
Third night running. I will sleep when somebody else is awake.
I am on my feet more than I am off them. It shows by the end.
Tired is the uniform. Nobody issued me a better one.
Do the walls still hold?
They hold. Somebody's grandfather paid for them and I get to stand on them.
They hold. The gate is the soft part and everybody knows it.
Stone does not ask much of you. That is more than I can say for the roster.
They have held longer than anyone alive. I would not be the one to test them.
How is the temple?
The roof leaks over the east aisle. We pray a little further west in wet weather.
Standing. Cold. Half of it needs money nobody here has.
The building is older than the town remembers, and it is starting to show.
Well enough. The lead wants replacing and the answer is always next year.
Busy morning?
Nobody has come in since dawn. That is either very good or very bad and I never learn which.
Two this morning, and both only wanted to sit. I let them.
Quiet. People come when something has gone wrong, so quiet is a kind of news.
Not busy. I have swept the same floor twice and I am considering a third.
Is this weather an omen?
Half the town will ask me that today. The honest answer is that it is weather.
Three have asked me already. I gave three answers and meant none of them.
If it is a sign, it is a poorly written one. Come inside out of it.
It is loud, and loud makes people religious. I take what I am given.
What is on today?
Small beer, and it is honest. The good barrel is not ready and I will not rush it.
Bread, broth, and whatever the pot has decided to become.
There is a stew. Do not ask me what week it started in.
Ale and a bed. If you want more than that you have come a long way for nothing.
How are the rooms?
Full. One of them snores like a saw and the other four have all told me so.
Clean, which is more than the last place you slept, I would guess.
There is one at the back. Small and quiet, and the better of the two.
Dry and warm. I make no promises about who is in the next bed.
Business good?
Good enough that I turned two away last night. I am not used to saying that.
Better than it has been. Money in the town means money over the bar.
I have stopped watering the beer. That is how you know.
Good. I keep waiting for it to stop, and it keeps not stopping.
How is the barley coming?
Slow. It always looks slow to me and then it is suddenly all at once.
Coming. Ask me in three weeks and I will have an opinion worth having.
Better than last year, which is not saying a great deal.
It is in the ground and it is up. Everything after that is weather.
Much to do?
The north fence again. Something keeps going through it and I have never once seen what.
There is always something. The day there is not, I will have died in the night.
Ditch wants clearing, gate wants hanging, and I want an hour sitting down.
Enough that I am talking to you instead of doing it.
Good weather for it?
This is the rain you want, if it stops. It is the not stopping that ruins you.
Good for the ground, bad for the back. That is most weather.
I asked for this a fortnight ago. I am not going to complain about getting it.
Rain now is worth more than sun in a month. Wet is fine.
Long day?
My back says so. My back has said so since I was twenty.
Started before light. I will finish after it, and be paid for neither end.
Long enough that I have stopped counting the loads.
Same as yesterday. Same as tomorrow, I should think.
What are you hauling?
Stone, up the hill, all of it. Whoever drew the plan never carried anything.
Timber today. Heavier than it looks and it looks heavy.
Sacks. Do not ask what is in them, I have stopped wondering.
Whatever is at the bottom of the cart when I get there.
Work in this cold?
Ground is frozen hard as iron. We dig anyway, just slower and for the same money.
Cold does not stop the work, it only stops the hands.
You warm up after the first hour. It is the first hour that is the trouble.
I would rather this than the heat. You can put more on in winter.
Good spot?
Best corner in town. Everyone walks past it and nobody looks at it. Suits me.
It is out of the wind, and that is most of what a spot is.
Good until the market moves. Then I move too, and quickly.
I have had worse. I have been moved off better.
Anyone bother you?
Only the dogs, and only because I feed them. My own fault entirely.
The watch, once a week, and never with any real heart in it.
Nobody. You have to be seen first, and I am not.
The children, mostly, and they are not the worst company I have had.
Are people generous here?
There is money in this town. Some of it even comes down as far as me.
Generous enough. It is easier to give when it does not cost you anything.
The well off give coin and the poor give bread. I know which I would rather have.
Some are. The ones with the least are the quickest, which I have never understood.
What are you playing?
You have to get to the well without touching the ground. I am the best at it.
We are hiding, but they are very bad at looking so I came out.
It does not have a name. You just have to do what I say.
I am counting. I have got to a hundred twice and nobody has come back.
Shouldn't you be somewhere?
Letters. I can do most of them. I am not going back until someone makes me.
Probably. Nobody has come looking yet.
I am supposed to be fetching water. I have been supposed to for a while now.
Do not tell anyone you saw me. That is the whole thing I am asking.
Cold enough for you?
It snowed! Nobody else is even excited. I do not understand grown people.
My hands do not work but I am not going in. They cannot make me.
I have been out since it started. I am going to be out until it stops.
It is the best thing that has happened all year and it is only the morning.
Do people fish here?
Off the point, when the tide is right. Half the town claims to know when that is.
Everybody does, and nobody admits how little they catch.
The boats go out before light. You can hear them from the walls if you are awake.
Enough to eat. Not enough to sell, most weeks.
Is the pass open?
It is, today. Ask again after the next weather and you may get a different answer.
Open. Whether it is passable is a different question and a longer one.
It is. Take the lower track anyway, whatever anyone tells you.
Open since the thaw. It will shut again and it never gives warning.
Anything in the woods?
Wolves, they say. I have lived here forty years and heard them twice.
Deer, mostly. Whatever else is in there has the sense to stay in there.
Something takes the lambs. Everyone has a name for it and no one has seen it.
Nothing that troubles you on the path. Off the path is your own business.
Is the river low?
Lower than it should be. The mill wheel is turning about half as fast as it likes.
Low. You can walk the ford without wetting your knees, which is wrong for the season.
Lower every year, and nobody upstream will admit to a thing.
It is low now and it will be over the bank by spring. It always does both.
Everything is mud.
Every year. Every single year, and every year we are all surprised by it.
Give it a fortnight. It goes from mud to dust and neither is any use.
Mud is the price of the thaw. I will take it over the frost.
Wipe your feet or do not, it makes no difference by noon.
Warm today.
Too warm to do anything and too bright to sleep. I will not complain again until tomorrow.
Warm. We were praying for this in the wet and now look at us.
Everyone is indoors till the shadows come round. You should be too.
Warm enough that the dogs have stopped moving. That is my measure.
Ready for the cold?
Getting the stores in. It is never quite as much as you remember needing.
Nearly. There is always one more thing that should have been done in summer.
Ready as we get. You find out in the second month whether you were right.
The roof is seen to and the wood is stacked. The rest is luck.
Enough firewood?
Enough if it breaks early. It has not broken early in my lifetime.
Enough. I said that last year too, and I was burning the fence by the end.
For now. Ask me again when the pile stops looking like a pile.
We have wood. What we do not have is anyone keen to go and cut more.
Who built the walls?
People who are all dead now. We live behind them and mostly forget they are there.
Whoever was frightened at the time. That is who builds a wall.
Nobody agrees. Everyone agrees it was not them, and that is as far as it goes.
They went up in a bad year. We have had good ones since and kept them anyway.
This place has seen trouble.
Once. You can still see where the old stone stops and the new stone starts.
It has. Nobody here brings it up, and nobody here has forgotten it either.
My grandmother was a girl for it. She would not speak of it and never stopped hinting.
Once was enough. We built back narrower and we built back higher.
Keeping well?
My knees tell me the weather now. They are more reliable than anyone in this town.
Well enough. Everything works, and everything complains about it.
I am upright and I am talking to you. That is a good day at my age.
Better than some. I have outlived two people who asked me that last winter.
How is the work?
I fetch things. Three years of fetching, I am told, and then I get to hold a tool.
I am learning. Mostly I am learning how much there is that I do not do yet.
Long days and not much of it mine. That is the arrangement and I signed it.
Good, when I am let near anything. I sweep a great deal.
Anything new in?
A little. It goes as fast as it lands, so ask early.
Whatever the last cart carried. I do not choose it, I only shelve it.
Less than I would like. The road has been slow this month.
Some. I put the good things at the back, out of honesty rather than cunning.
Do you give credit?
To people I have known longer than you. No offence in it.
I did once. I keep the list to remind myself not to.
Coin today, friendship tomorrow. It works better that way round.
For a neighbour, sometimes. For a traveller, never - you leave and the debt stays.
How is the oven?
Hot and staying that way. It takes half the night to get there.
Even, today. Some days one side takes against me.
Old. Older than the house round it, and better built.
Hungry. It eats more wood than the town thinks it does.
Up early?
Before the birds, most days. Bread will not wait for daylight.
Always. The town wakes to it and never wonders when it started.
I have forgotten what the morning looks like from the other side of it.
Early enough that I am ready for bed when you are ready for lunch.
How is the wheel running?
True, this week. Ask me again after the rain.
Well enough. A wheel tells you long before it stops.
Slow. The water is low and there is nothing to be done about it.
Sweetly. There is no sound like it when it is right.
Does the dust bother you?
Not any more. That is either habit or something worse.
It gets in everything. My wife knows me by the grey.
You stop seeing it. You never stop tasting it.
Less than fire does. Flour dust and a spark do not mix, and everyone forgets that.
Has anything been happening?
Something big was killed out past the ridge. Folk went to look and came back quiet.
There was a thing out there. Somebody put it down. I have not been out that way since.

Nothing has been over this ground.
